labeling.basis: Goal and frozen public types/contract, plus cited declaration specifications; discovery/comparison implementations and outputs were not read to derive labels.
labeling.sourceNature: Synthetic local projects only. Source URLs are metadata and are never fetched by tests.
labeling.scope: Finite supported workflow agreement, not field accuracy or complete project coverage.

independentReview.scope: All 21 case rationales, snapshot expectations, 22 comparison change labels, and all 24 synthetic fixture file contents were reviewed before evaluator execution.
independentReview.rationale: The reviewer did not implement discovery/comparison. Labels agree with the frozen goal and public contract: exact current pointers survive supported reordering, unrelated known evidence remains comparable, and moves/incompatible semantics remain separate unknown observations.
independentReview.fixtureConstraintCorrection: Before API execution, author and independent reviewer agreed that exact-cap discovery may conservatively remain incomplete. The complete side of two capped-inventory pairs uses maxEntries:2 rather than 1; the incomplete side retains 1. All comparison labels, pointers, and counts are unchanged.

coverage.additionalIntegrationOwner: Root CLI tests: reject existing snapshot outputs, preserve source inputs, and validate/execute the local CI example. The corpus checks portable Unicode evidence and input immutability.

cases.rationale: Conventional Compose and OpenAPI filenames in different folders are selected; unrelated project metadata stays ignored. Both explicit declarations remain observable.
An explicit root-relative selector admits the nonstandard contract name. Unicode in the project and file paths is preserved as private evidence metadata.
The default generated build tree and explicitly excluded vendor tree must not contribute observations. Deliberate skipped scope stays visible; the remaining Compose file is assessed.
A complete inventory containing only unrelated README and package metadata is a valid empty supported-file result; it does not establish project security.
The same file is fully assessed on both sides, and the candidate newly requests privileged mode.
Complete compatible baseline discovery establishes that the candidate's conventional Compose file did not exist within the same scope. Its declaration is new, unlike a missing baseline snapshot.
Reordering mapping fields and adding harmless labels preserve the same explicit privilege declaration. Absolute fixture roots and bytes differ without changing declaration identity.
The candidate fully assesses the same file/rule and contains explicit false in place of true. Report removal of this declaration, not deployed remediation.

Capability list order, security alternative order and required-scope order do not change the supported declarations. Match their semantic identities while retaining exact current array-index evidence.
A deleted configuration file does not demonstrate removal from a still-assessed declaration or deployed remediation. Retain the baseline observation with unknown change status.
Identical content moved between paths is ambiguous under the bounded rename policy. The frozen contract exposes separate before-only and after-only unknown records, without a fabricated introduction.
Unresolved baseline interpolation prevents establishing introduction for that file/rule. A separate fully assessed capability declaration still compares unchanged.
Unresolved candidate interpolation prevents establishing removal. Unrelated compatible evidence remains comparable instead of discarding the whole project's known observations.

An entry limit of one stops baseline discovery among two unrelated files. The supported-file inventory is empty but incomplete, so it cannot prove absence of the candidate declaration. A limit of two allows the one-file candidate project to establish complete inventory without depending on EOF behavior at the exact cap; selection policy is unchanged.

An entry limit of one stops candidate discovery among two unrelated files. Empty observed inventory cannot support a removal claim. A limit of two permits complete inventory of the one-file baseline project; its declaration evidence remains unknown while candidate discovery is incomplete. The selection policy is unchanged.
Changing a snapshot ID without resealing breaks its content identity. Invalid snapshots are rejected with failed comparison and no asserted changes.
A valid resealed snapshot with a different exclusion policy has incompatible selected scope. Each side's observation remains a separate unknown record; no introduction/removal is asserted.
A valid resealed snapshot from different reviewer semantics cannot establish a trustworthy delta. Change only the digest dynamically; no current engine fingerprint is hard-coded.
A one-file ceiling cannot silently classify a project with two conventional candidates as fully covered.
A byte ceiling smaller than either candidate prevents analysis and must remain explicit incomplete discovery rather than a completed empty project.
The directory-entry ceiling bounds inventory itself. Partial traversal cannot establish absence even if no observation was emitted.
